ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $AB$ is a tangent to the circle $\odot O$ with $A$ as the point of tangency. The line $OB$ intersects $\odot O$ at point $C$. Point $D$ is on the circle $\odot O$. Connect $AD$, $CD$, and $OA$. If $\angle ADC=25^\circ$, what is the degree measure of $\angle ABO$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that $AB$ is the tangent of circle $O$,

it follows that $AB \perp OA$,

which implies $\angle OAB = 90^\circ$.

Given that $\angle ADC = 25^\circ$,

it follows that $\angle AOB = 2\angle ADC = 50^\circ$,

therefore, $\angle ABO = 90^\circ - 50^\circ = \boxed{40^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is circle ⊙O, O is inside the circle; A is near the lower side of the circle, AB is a horizontal tangent line passing through A and extending left to B; OA connects to the point of tangency A. The straight line OB goes from B through C on the circle and then to O, so C is on ray OB. D is at the lower right of the circle, and AD and CD are connected in the figure. Reasoning: ∠ADC is an inscribed angle, and what it subtends is arc AC, therefore the central angle ∠AOC subtending the same arc AC = 2×∠ADC = 2×25° = 50°. Because C is on straight line OB, and viewed from O the direction of OC is consistent with OB, ∠AOB = ∠AOC = 50°. Also because AB is the tangent line to the circle at point A, radius OA is perpendicular to tangent line AB, so ∠OAB = 90°. In triangle AOB, ∠ABO = 180° - 90° - 50° = 40°.
